chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: “Indeed, knowledge is inherited, and no knowledgeable one dies except that he leaves behind one who knows the like of his knowledge, or whatever Allah wills.”

key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: knowledge, especially divinely guided and inherited knowledge
key_terms.يُتَوَارَثُ: is inherited and passed down from one to another

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام describe the inheritance of sacred knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith states that true divinely guided knowledge is transmitted continuously and does not disappear with the death of a scholar. It points to the ongoing inheritance of sacred knowledge, especially through those appointed to preserve and convey it by the will of Allah.
